newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba-Bund mkt trend set by U.S. only in short term.
newsitem.headline: Buba-Bund mkt trend set by U.S. only in short term.

text.p: Trends in the German bond market are now often dictated by market movements in the short term, but studies show the market is driven by domestic factors if observed over a longer period, the Bundesbank said.

In its July monthly report, published on Wednesday, the central bank said that the results of an empirical study showed that the central bank's best course of monetary policy action was therefore to stick by a steady, mid-term oriented policy.

Noting that the influence of monetary policy on capital markets lay in inflation expectations and the inflation risk premium, the Bundesbank said a consistent anti-inflationary strategy was thus the best approach.

"The aim from the point of view of the central bank is to keep both of these interest rate components as low as possible, so that the expectations they reflect are in line with the goal of achieving long-term price stability," the report said.
"This can only be achieved if the formation of interest rate conditions in the money market is embedded in a consistent and credible monetary policy strategy.
"If this can be achieved, the central bank can make a significant contribution to reducing uncertainty with respect to the long-term interest rate trend," it said.
In particular, the central bank warned that it would be unwise for monetary policy to take a short-term approach with the express aim of countering external trends and influences.
"The consequence is that the central bank should not attempt to offset undesirable external influences on the capital market with a short-term counter action," it said.
The Bundesbank warned that such an approach could in fact disturb the long-term stability of the market.

The central bank study showed that the relationship between U.S. capital market rates had clearly grown stronger since the 1980s, partly due to the general globalisation trend and resulting integration of world markets.
"The study shows that the interest rate bond with the United States has grown markedly closer since the start of the 1980s," it said.

"In the longer term German capital market rates continue to be determined by domestic factors; in the short term, on the contrary, the German interest rate trend generally follows the U.S. market," it said.
The central bank's study observed capital market rates over a 23-year period, from February 1974 to December 1996.
